A common path is to apprentice at a drilling or well company, carry rods and learn from experienced drillers, earn relevant rig-operating certificates, lead a rig independently, and then learn geological logging and drilling-fluid formulation.
This career suits resilient, careful people who tolerate field life. If you can stay engaged in remote areas and monitor one rig all day without losing focus, the field welcomes you.

Earth Drillers, Except Oil And Gas operate rigs to drill water wells, geothermal wells, geological exploration holes, and environmental-monitoring holes in soil and rock. They set up equipment, drill and sample, stabilize and flush holes, and maintain records that bring subsurface information to the surface.

entries: Earth Drillers operate rigs in soil and rock to create water wells, geothermal wells, geological exploration holes, and environmental-monitoring holes. They set up equipment, drill and sample, stabilize and flush holes, and maintain records that bring subsurface information to the surface.
Operate rigs and adjust speed, pressure, and drilling-fluid mixtures as formations change.
Erect and dismantle derricks, connect rods, and replace bits and samplers.
Pump fluid or air into holes to stabilize walls, clean holes, cool tools, and remove cuttings.
Extract cores, soil, or groundwater samples and log and preserve them on site.
Record borehole depth, formation descriptions, footage, and equipment operations.
Maintain rigs and supporting equipment and resolve stuck pipe, collapse, and other field failures.

paragraphs: The day's rhythm is rotation, pressure, flushing, and logging. Drillers start the rig and judge formation hardness through sound and instruments. They change bits for hard layers and adjust pressure for soft layers. Drilling fluid carries cuttings out. At design depth, crews retrieve and label cores. After each hole, they relocate equipment and complete records at night.

In one sentence: they move a rig to a location, drill underground rod by rod, recover core and soil samples, and secure the borehole. Tasks include rig operation, derrick setup, bit changes, drilling-fluid stabilization, sampling and logging, borehole records, and equipment maintenance.

Employment is projected to rise to 18,800 by 2034, a net increase of about 500 jobs, with about 1,700 openings each year. Median annual pay was about $59,600 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace Earth Drillers, Except Oil And Gas, but it will change how crews understand subsurface conditions. Automatic records and real-time data transfer simplify logging. Operators still control the rig, judge drilling fluid by feel, and respond to stuck pipe. Most work happens in the field; AI reaches the data, not the drill floor.

paragraphs: A score of 4/10 places this occupation in the low-moderate AI exposure range. Most work happens in the field, leaving few desk tasks for algorithms beyond records and data organization.

Low-moderate exposure still brings change. Automatic logging and measurement while drilling are reaching worksites. Drillers who understand instruments and data will be more valuable than workers who rely only on physical effort. Manual drilling without proper records faces the greatest pressure.

Study drilling or engineering at a vocational school and seek field placements. Young drillers who interpret measurement-while-drilling data and maintain smart rigs are in demand, so accept a difficult start.

Master automatic logging and measurement-while-drilling instruments, and learn basic geotechnical engineering. Combine drilling with data interpretation to gain bargaining power in geothermal and environmental work.

Do not write only that you can operate a rig. State that you can read borehole logs, describe stuck-pipe or collapse incidents you resolved, and report monthly drilling footage. Certificates help, and dependable workers are welcome.
Do not hire for strength alone. Assess safety habits and data awareness. Drillers who independently lead a rig, produce compliant logs, and use basic instruments merit higher rig-day rates.

Oil and gas drillers create petroleum and natural-gas wells using larger rigs and more industrialized, automated processes. Earth Drillers create water wells, geothermal wells, and geological exploration holes with more flexible equipment and greater reliance on distributed field judgment.

Not as a whole. AI and automatic records handle logging and data organization, while measurement-while-drilling systems assist formation assessment. People still operate rigs, adjust drilling fluid, and resolve stuck pipe. Data-blind working methods face the greatest pressure.
